principles: Do not add a new capability layer for presentation value.
Only distinguish proof tiers where the distinction prevents a real overclaim.
Keep the execution plan mechanically verifiable through Lattice lifecycle evidence.
Preserve Layer3 claim boundaries and keep Production Safety/global claims locked.
drivers: The existing formal UDM unlock did not execute real Story lifecycle scenarios.
The user needs a plan that avoids inflated capability claims.
The document should be executable by future Lattice stories and host-neutral audits.

options.name: A: Create a separate real execution UDM decision document
pros: Avoids hiding the correction inside an existing long document
cons: Adds one more decision document that must be linked from future Layer3 work

options.name: B: Patch only the existing Layer3 formal unlock document
pros: Keeps all Layer3 text in one place
cons: Can blur formal proof path and real execution proof
Makes it harder to audit exactly what the second-tier plan requires

chosen: A: Create a separate real execution UDM decision document
rationale: Choose a separate document because the user identified a real correctness issue in the claim boundary: formal artifacts are not the same as real lifecycle execution. A dedicated execution plan keeps the correction visible and auditable without changing the already-valid formal unlock path.

preMortem.scenario: The document accidentally implies Production Safety is unlocked by real UDM execution.
preMortem.trigger: Allowed wording says production-grade or arbitrary unattended development.
preMortem.consequence: Capability claim becomes inflated and inconsistent with Layer4 locks.
preMortem.mitigation: Include explicit claim boundaries and prohibited wording.

preMortem.scenario: The document defines synthetic artifact generation again instead of real lifecycle runs.
preMortem.trigger: Pass criteria reference only final-report artifacts and not Story phases or gate evidence.
preMortem.consequence: The second-tier plan fails to fix the user-raised correctness gap.
preMortem.mitigation: Require real story_create through DONE/BLOCKED runs for key UDM scenarios.

preMortem.scenario: The plan becomes too broad and delays useful validation.
preMortem.trigger: It requires every UDM baseline to be a full product build before any claim can improve.
preMortem.consequence: The work becomes bulky and violates no-arbitrary-optimization principle.
preMortem.mitigation: Use a minimal required set of real execution scenarios plus mapping to the 10 UDM IDs.
